gpt-image-1.5.note: OpenAI. Explicit input_fidelity ('high' to hold a face, 'low' to dial it down — gpt-image-2 cannot). Aspect limited to 1:1/3:2/2:3. The one that does transparent backgrounds.

background.transparent: gpt-image-2 does not support transparent backgrounds (its schema still lists the value). Use gpt-image-1.5 for transparent PNGs.

gpt-image-2.note: OpenAI; the default for character frames. Strong instruction-following and legible text; widest aspect list, including explicit pixel sizes. Reference images are held at HIGH FIDELITY AUTOMATICALLY — the input_fidelity knob is absent because it is always on, not because it was lost.

grok-imagine-video.note: xAI Grok Imagine Video (Aurora). Native synced audio incl. lip-sync. Two things nothing else here does: a true duration RANGE (1-15s, not an enum) and a video-EDITING mode via the `video` input (max 8.7s in, output matches its duration/ratio/resolution). No reference images and no last frame. NEGATIVE DIRECTION IS IGNORED — the model has no negative_prompt field and the README says prompt-embedded negatives are dropped too; describe what you want instead. accepts_ext confirmed by the README.

image-upscale.note: The only model here that RESTORES rather than generates: it enlarges an image that already exists and invents nothing, so it is what seed and reference material goes through. `High Fidelity V2` preserves detail, `Low Resolution V2` is for badly degraded sources, and `face_enhancement_creativity: 0` sharpens a face without redrawing it. Priced on OUTPUT megapixels, not runtime.

kling.note: Kling 3.0 / O3 Omni. Pay-per-second, no resource package. Start frame AND reference images can be combined. Native multi-shot to 6 cuts (durations must sum to `duration`, else E006). Rejects .webp.

nano-banana-2.note: Google, Gemini 3.1 Flash Image. Faster/cheaper sibling of Pro; 1K default. Adds the extreme 1:4/4:1/1:8/8:1 aspect ratios and Google Search / Image Search grounding.

nano-banana-pro.note: Google, built on Gemini 3 Pro. 2K default, up to 4K. Tunable safety_filter_level and match_input_image aspect. Docs: holds resemblance for up to 5 people across a composition.

seedance.note: ByteDance Seedance 2.0. Native audio, first/last frame, reference images/videos/audio. A first frame and a reference set CANNOT be combined.

seedance-2.5.note: ByteDance Seedance 2.5, the successor to seedance (2.0): native synced audio with better dialogue timing and lip-sync, a true 30 s ceiling in one pass (duration 4-30, or -1 to let the model choose), reference sets of up to 30 images / 10 videos / 10 audios, and an `adaptive` aspect ratio. On Replicate it renders at 480p or 720p ONLY - no 1080p or 4k tier - at $0.1028/s and $0.2312/s (about x4 with a reference video). A first frame still CANNOT be combined with references; first+last-frame, editing and extension modes require aspect_ratio adaptive. Has a seed (not guaranteed). Prefer it over seedance for anything spoken.

size.1.5K: seedream-5-pro renders standard images at 1K or 2K only; 1.5K exists for layer_decomposition mode (its schema lists it for both).
size.auto: seedream-5-pro renders standard images at 1K or 2K only; auto exists for layer_decomposition mode, where it sizes from the input image.

seedream-5-pro.note: ByteDance's flagship image model. 1K/2K only (2K default, ~4MP), up to 10 reference images for character/style/product consistency and multi-image composition; aspect defaults to match_input_image. Flat per-image pricing. Also has a layer_decomposition mode that splits one image into a base plus up to 16 element layers.

veo-3.1.note: Google Veo 3.1. Native synced audio, 24 fps, SynthID watermark. The only video engine here with a SEED and with negative_prompt as a real parameter. reference_images caps at 3 and ONLY works at aspect_ratio 16:9 with duration 8 — the schema still accepts other combinations and silently drops the reference set. A last_frame is ignored when reference_images are present. accepts_ext unverified: the README names no formats.

krea-2-large.note: Krea 2 Large. Krea's flagship still model: photorealism, natural light, textured and expressive looks; `creativity` raw/low/medium/high sets how far it embellishes the prompt; has a SEED (as does flux-2-pro). `style_reference_images` (<=10) is a STYLE transfer input, NOT an identity reference: --character binds a likeness into it and the model keeps the look, not the face. No output-format, size or quality knob; flat $0.06/image (+$0.005 with style refs, +$0.01 with a Krea moodboard).

gpt-image-2.5-sunburst.note: OpenAI, tuned for EDITING PRECISION (gpt-image-2.5-flare is the same model line tuned for speed, at the same prices): targeted changes that keep identity, composition and lighting; dense text. Same schema as gpt-image-2 plus two quality tiers, `xhigh` and `max`, and its README endorses `background: transparent` (gpt-image-2's does not, so no `denied` here). References held at high fidelity automatically. Priced PER QUALITY TIER: low $0.012, medium $0.047, high $0.128, xhigh $0.25, max $0.50 — and `auto`, the schema default, bills at the xhigh rate, which is why the registry defaults quality to medium.

gpt-image-2.5-flare.note: OpenAI's FASTEST image model, the high-volume sibling of gpt-image-2.5-sunburst. Identical schema, identical per-tier prices (low $0.012, medium $0.047, high $0.128, xhigh $0.25, max $0.50; `auto` bills at the xhigh rate, hence the medium default) and an identical README minus 'editing precision matters most' — Sunburst is the one to pay for when the edit must be exact; Flare is for drafts, iteration and volume. References held at high fidelity automatically; `background: transparent` endorsed.

kling-v3-motion-control.note: Kling 3.0 Motion Control. Transfers the CHARACTER MOTION of a reference clip onto one still: `image` is the look (one .jpg/.jpeg/.png, 340-3850px, ratio 1:2.5..2.5:1, <=10MB), `video` is the motion (.mp4/.mov, <=100MB) and is REQUIRED. No duration, aspect_ratio, reference_images or last frame: length and framing follow the reference clip. `character_orientation` image = faces as in the still, clip <=10s; video = faces as in the clip, clip <=30s. `mode` std=720p, pro=1080p. `keep_original_sound` carries the clip's audio over. Bind the clip with --clip-run/--clip-key.

flux-2-pro.note: FLUX.2 [pro], Black Forest Labs' production still model: text-to-image, natural-language EDITING of up to 8 input_images (address them by index — 'the beach in image 3'), legible text/typography, photorealism, character and product consistency across the reference set; JSON-structured prompts are documented. `seed` for repeatable draws. `resolution` 0.5/1/2/4 MP (2 MP or below recommended; 2048px hard cap per side) or `aspect_ratio: custom` + width/height in multiples of 16; `match_input_image` on both follows the FIRST input image. Total input ≤9 MP. No negative prompts — the README says they can add what they exclude. Priced per megapixel: $0.015 per run + $0.015 per input MP + $0.015 per output MP (a 1 MP still with no refs ≈ $0.03; 2 MP ≈ $0.045).

z-image-turbo.note: Z-Image Turbo, Tongyi Lab's distilled 6B text-to-image model, called on Runpod's public endpoint (not through Replicate): eight-step generation in a few seconds, photorealism, bilingual (English/Chinese) text rendering, a prompt enhancer that expands short prompts — so write a descriptive sentence, not a tag list. `image` (one URL) switches it to image-to-image, with `strength` 0–1 (default 0.8) for how far to depart from it. `size` is a fixed list of `W*H` strings, 1024*1024 by default; `seed` -1 is random, any other value repeats a draw. No negative prompt, no step count — it is distilled to eight and more steps make it worse. Flat $0.005 per image whatever the size, failed generations free, output URLs kept about seven days. The one model here whose run record carries a real price.

wan-2.6-t2v.note: Alibaba's Wan 2.6, text-to-video, on Runpod's public endpoint (not Replicate) — the first open-weight video model here and the first video model that takes no image at all. Prose prompt in, a 5/10/15 s clip out at 720p or 1080p, landscape or portrait (`size` is W*H); `shot_type: multi` lets it cut between shots inside one clip; a real `negative_prompt`; a repeatable `seed`. `enable_prompt_expansion` hands the prompt to a rewriter first and is off by default. No reference images, no start or end frame — for those use wan-2.6-i2v. Priced per clip, not per second: 720p $0.50 / $1.00 / $1.50 and 1080p $0.75 / $1.50 / $2.25 for 5 / 10 / 15 s (Runpod, September 2026); the run records the price. The endpoint's optional `audio` URL is not wired — studio binds nodes, never URLs. Output URL lasts seven days; the run stores the bytes. The worker validates `size` (the four W*H values) and `duration` (5/10/15) and IGNORES any field it does not know — a misspelt input is not refused, it renders at the default and bills, so the registry's check is the only one there is.

wan-2.6-i2v.note: Alibaba's Wan 2.6, image-to-video, on Runpod's public endpoint (not Replicate): one still in (`image`, bound with --start-run / --start-key), a 5/10/15 s clip out that opens on that frame, at `resolution` 720p or 1080p, landscape. **Runpod's own page is wrong about this endpoint's inputs** — it documents `size` as W*H; the worker (`Wan_2.6_I2VInput`) takes `resolution` in `720p`/`1080p` and refuses anything else, and it REQUIRES `shot_type`, which the registry defaults to `single`. Measured 2026-09-16 from the worker's validation errors, after a run sent `size: 1920*1080` and failed. Same other controls as wan-2.6-t2v — a real `negative_prompt`, a repeatable `seed`, `enable_prompt_expansion` off by default — plus `enable_safety_checker`. No reference list: identity comes from the frame, which is the frame-first workflow every other video engine here uses. Priced per second of output: $0.10/s at 720p, $0.15/s at 1080p (Runpod, September 2026), so a 5 s 720p clip is $0.50; the run records the price. The endpoint's optional `audio` URL is not wired — studio binds nodes, never URLs. Output URL lasts seven days; the run stores the bytes.

wan-2.2-i2v-lora.note: Wan 2.2 image-to-video at 720p WITH YOUR OWN LoRA, on Runpod's public endpoint (its id is `wan-2-2-t2v-720-lora` although it takes an image — the docs' table links a name that does not exist). The one model here that loads weights that are not its own: `high_noise_loras` and `low_noise_loras` each take a list of `{path, scale}`, one adapter per denoising stage the way Wan 2.2's two-expert sampler wants them. In studio a LoRA is a SEND — a `.safetensors` node in the library, bound with --lora-high-key / --lora-low-key, presigned at submit — never a pasted URL (hard rule #3); `lora_scale` is studio's one number for every adapter's `scale`. One required start frame (`image`), no reference list, no negative prompt, no size field (720p landscape). 5 or 8 seconds; $0.35 / $0.56 per clip (Runpod, September 2026). The destination for a trained character LoRA, and the untrained-with-a-public-LoRA baseline before one exists.

wan-3.0-t2v.note: Alibaba's Wan 3.0, text-to-video, on fal.ai's queue API (the third provider: `provider: fal`, `model: fal/<endpoint>`; neither Replicate nor Runpod hosts Wan 3.0 in September 2026). Prose prompt in, a clip of 2–30 s out at 480p/720p/1080p in any of five aspect ratios, with native audio. No image input of any kind — for a start or end frame use wan-3.0-i2v, for reference images wan-3.0-r2v. The schema is live: fal publishes an OpenAPI document per endpoint and `models show`/`refresh` read it. Priced per second of output by resolution: $0.05/s at 480p, $0.10/s at 720p, $0.20/s at 1080p (fal, September 2026) — a 5 s clip is $0.25 / $0.50 / $1.00 — and fal's body carries no price, so `cost.amount` stays null; fal's dashboard is the bill. The registry defaults `resolution` to 720p for that reason (fal's own default is 1080p). `duration` is any integer 2–30, or null for the model to pick a length from the prompt; `aspect_ratio` is `adaptive` by default and takes 16:9 / 4:3 / 1:1 / 3:4 / 9:16. `audio` (on by default) generates a soundtrack in the same pass. `enable_prompt_expansion` is left ON, unlike the Wan 2.6 entries, because fal says turning it off degrades the result — the rewritten prompt comes back as `actual_prompt` and the run stores the response, so what was actually sent to the model is on the record. `enable_thinking` (off) adds a reasoning pass and latency. A repeatable `seed`; no negative prompt field — keep-outs go in the prompt. Output URL is fal's CDN; the run stores the bytes.

wan-3.0-i2v.note: Alibaba's Wan 3.0, image-to-video, on fal.ai's queue API (`provider: fal`). One REQUIRED start frame (`start_image_url`, bound with --start-run / --start-key) and an optional last frame (`end_image_url`, --end-run / --end-key) the clip lands on — the frame-first workflow every other video engine here uses, plus the interpolation only Veo and Seedance also offer. 2–30 s, 480p/720p/1080p, native audio; `aspect_ratio: adaptive` follows the frame. No reference list: identity comes from the frame. Live schema from fal's OpenAPI document. Priced per second of output by resolution: $0.05/s at 480p, $0.10/s at 720p, $0.20/s at 1080p (fal, September 2026) — a 5 s clip is $0.25 / $0.50 / $1.00 — and fal's body carries no price, so `cost.amount` stays null; fal's dashboard is the bill. The registry defaults `resolution` to 720p for that reason (fal's own default is 1080p). `duration` is any integer 2–30, or null for the model to pick a length from the prompt; `aspect_ratio` is `adaptive` by default and takes 16:9 / 4:3 / 1:1 / 3:4 / 9:16. `audio` (on by default) generates a soundtrack in the same pass. `enable_prompt_expansion` is left ON, unlike the Wan 2.6 entries, because fal says turning it off degrades the result — the rewritten prompt comes back as `actual_prompt` and the run stores the response, so what was actually sent to the model is on the record. `enable_thinking` (off) adds a reasoning pass and latency. A repeatable `seed`; no negative prompt field — keep-outs go in the prompt. Output URL is fal's CDN; the run stores the bytes.

wan-3.0-r2v.note: Alibaba's Wan 3.0, reference-to-video, on fal.ai's queue API (`provider: fal`). Up to 10 reference images (`reference_image_urls`, bound with --character / --ref-run / --key) that the prompt addresses positionally — 'the subject in Image 1 walks past…' — which is what makes it the Wan engine for a character on-model, the role Kling's and Seedance's reference lists play. No start or end frame: the references steer identity and the prompt steers the shot. 2–30 s, 480p/720p/1080p, native audio. The endpoint also takes up to 5 reference videos and 5 reference audios and a `web_url`/`file_url` to build from; none is wired — studio binds image nodes, never URLs, and no clip or audio send exists for this entry yet. Live schema from fal's OpenAPI document. Priced per second of output by resolution: $0.05/s at 480p, $0.10/s at 720p, $0.20/s at 1080p (fal, September 2026) — a 5 s clip is $0.25 / $0.50 / $1.00 — and fal's body carries no price, so `cost.amount` stays null; fal's dashboard is the bill. The registry defaults `resolution` to 720p for that reason (fal's own default is 1080p). `duration` is any integer 2–30, or null for the model to pick a length from the prompt; `aspect_ratio` is `adaptive` by default and takes 16:9 / 4:3 / 1:1 / 3:4 / 9:16. `audio` (on by default) generates a soundtrack in the same pass. `enable_prompt_expansion` is left ON, unlike the Wan 2.6 entries, because fal says turning it off degrades the result — the rewritten prompt comes back as `actual_prompt` and the run stores the response, so what was actually sent to the model is on the record. `enable_thinking` (off) adds a reasoning pass and latency. A repeatable `seed`; no negative prompt field — keep-outs go in the prompt. Output URL is fal's CDN; the run stores the bytes.

wan-3.0-openrouter.note: Alibaba's Wan 3.0 through OpenRouter (the fourth provider: `provider: openrouter`, `model: openrouter/<slug>`), the same model as the fal `wan-3.0-*` entries routed straight to Alibaba — registered beside them so a run can be priced on either. ONE entry for two modes: text-to-video with no image, image-to-video with an optional `first_frame` (bound with --start-run / --start-key; sent as OpenRouter's `frame_images`). No end frame and no reference list — OpenRouter's card for this model offers `first_frame` only, so for an end frame use wan-3.0-i2v and for references wan-3.0-r2v, both on fal. No `negative_prompt`, no prompt-expansion switch, no thinking pass: OpenRouter forwards no passthrough parameters for this model, so keep-outs go in the prompt. 2–30 s (`duration`, an integer; the registry defaults 5), 480p/720p/1080p (`resolution`, defaulted to 720p), five aspect ratios (16:9 / 4:3 / 1:1 / 3:4 / 9:16, no `adaptive`), `generate_audio` on by default, a repeatable `seed`. Schema is live, synthesised from OpenRouter's model card. List price per second of output: $0.05 at 480p, $0.10 at 720p, $0.20 at 1080p (OpenRouter, September 2026), with a 15% discount OpenRouter advertises on this route that the card does not print. Measured 2026-09-18 on the first live run: a 2 s 480p clip cost $0.2125 = 5 s × $0.05 × 0.85 — the discount is real and the clip is BILLED AS AT LEAST 5 SECONDS, so anything shorter costs the same as 5 s; at 5 s and above this is 15% under fal. The body carries `usage.cost`, so every run records what was actually charged. Output is fetched from OpenRouter's own content route with the key; the run stores the bytes.

Each prompt adds ~20 sampler steps of a 14B model per save point (about a minute on an A100).

wan-2.2-lora-train.note: Not a model: a TRAINER. Rents a Runpod GPU pod from the official ai-toolkit image, trains a Wan 2.2 14B LoRA pair (high-noise and low-noise experts, the pair `wan-2.2-i2v-lora` loads) on the character's images tagged `dataset`, uploads every checkpoint pair into `<character>/models/` and, at every save point, one sample still per `sample_prompts` entry into `<character>/models/samples/` (the run page shows them beside the pair), and terminates the pod. Captions are each file's description with the trigger in front — scene only, never the face. No prompt. Billed by the hour: an A100 80GB is ~$1.59/h and 2000 steps take roughly 1–2 h plus ~15 min of setup, so ~$3–5 an attempt; the run records pod-hours × rate. `max_hours` caps it on the pod itself. Runs ONLY where the API can reach Runpod's pod API and receive a callback; locally `studio runs reconcile` reads the pod's result from the bucket.
